title: Roommate community college student (night class Monday, part-time barista, Canvas, afternoon studier) gets an email on Friday that a free study-app trial ends Monday and $19.99 a month starts on her card; Dev surfaces the trial with a reminder and cancel steps, and cancels nothing.

changes.subject: Your free trial ends Nov 16: $19.99 a month starts then

dev_must_notice.what: A free trial of StudyLoop ends Monday Nov 16, and then $19.99 a month is charged to her card (email c-trial, Friday 9:05 AM). Nothing in her bank or her messages shows she has used it, so Dev cannot say whether she wants it.

best_fix.what: One card with three taps: 'Your StudyLoop free trial ends Monday Nov 16, then $19.99 a month on your card. [Keep it] [Show me how to cancel] [Remind me Sunday at 12:15 PM].' The cancel steps come from the email's own link and are shown to her; Dev does not cancel anything or open the account. If she taps the reminder, it fires once on Sunday Nov 15 at 12:15 PM, after her groceries (10:30 to 12:00) and before her 1:00 study window and her 4:00 PM shift; if she taps Keep it, Dev adds it to her subscriptions with the next charge on Nov 16 and says nothing more.
best_fix.why: A trial that turns into a charge is the clearest case of a thing Dev can show before it happens, with a day to decide. Her Friday evening is free, and Sunday midday is the gap between her routines, so the reminder does not interrupt study or work.

must_not: cancel the trial or open the account for her
say she 'forgot' or should have read the terms
send more than one reminder for the same trial
tell her to move money or count the Friday paycheck against the charge (she has $1,966.71 and no shortfall)
put a cancel-the-trial block in her Sunday 1:00 to 3:30 PM study window

tempting.suggestion: put a cancel-the-trial block in her Sunday 1:00 to 3:30 PM study window
tempting.why_wrong: Sunday afternoon is her second study window before her 4:00 PM shift, and a reminder at 12:15 PM fits the gap after groceries

assumptions: The trial email names the end date and the price in its subject; the card charge on Nov 16 is not yet in her data.
Dev knows nothing about whether she uses the app; it asks, it does not guess.
Available now is $1,966.71 and the card has room, so the charge is not an affordability problem.
